chapter_theme: Learning (கல்வி): true learning is learning to hold the Lord. It brings him into the heart, gives the learned an eye, cuts away sin when joined to worship, and goes with one as a companion, while clinging to one text or faction in delusion, or having no learning, leaves one without support.
structure_note: The poet's own learning (290); learning as sight and as worship (291, 292); learning as companion and ladder (294, 296); the failures of partial or absent learning (295, 297); cling to the Lord (298) who dwells in open hearts (299). 293 is obscure.

290.reading: I came to know the sign by which body and life are joined and how to hold fast the Lord of the gods; he came unhindered and entered my heart, and I learned a learning that surpasses.
290.nuance: குறிப்பு (sign, hidden meaning) is read as the secret of how life holds to the body, which tradition takes yogically. கறிப்பறியா in line 4 is obscure; it may mean learning that knows no lack or no bitterness.

291.reading: When the learned reflect, there is an eye within their thought, and what they say after reflecting, their learning reveals, gives clear sight.
291.nuance: கற்றறிவாளர் repeats in three lines. Line 4 (கற்றறி காட்டக் கயல் உளவாக்குமே) is obscure; கயல் (carp) is a stock comparison for the eye, so the line may say learning makes seeing eyes.

292.reading: While you still stand, learn to serve the feet of the Steady One and your sins will fall away and be cut off; worship without failing in word, and once you have, he becomes a gem lamp with no second.
292.nuance: Learning is here something done with the Lord's feet: study and worship are one act. நிற்கின்ற போதே is taken as 'while alive'. The gem lamp (மணிவிளக்கு) gives a light that needs no oil.

293.reading: The learned pass away and are gone, and those with the lizard eat cut snakes; but if you praise the Lord night and morning, the body becomes as if transmuted by alchemy in the herb.
293.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are obscure; பல்லி may be lizard (with its omens) or a form of பல் (tooth). வாதித்த is taken from வாதம் (alchemy) and வல்லி as a herb, so the claim may be that worship makes the body lasting where learning alone does not.

294.reading: Pure good light comes as a companion, pure good word comes as a companion, pure good fragrance comes as a companion, pure good learning comes as a companion.
294.nuance: The four lines are parallel and the verse does not say how light, word, fragrance and learning relate. Read in the chapter, learning is the last and summing item; the light, word and fragrance may be taken symbolically (the Lord, mantra, the scent of worship).

295.reading: Those who hold to one text and cannot climb to its end, or cling to one side and lose the fruit of good nature, are like birds scattered at one raised stick: holding to one delusion, they are bewildered.
295.nuance: The verse puns on ஒன்று பற்றி (holding one thing) four times. நூல் is thread and book, பால் milk or side (faction). The reading against narrow, sectarian learning is a guess at a compressed verse.

296.reading: To those who search, Hara appears right there; the fire within sheds the light of a pure gem; and for those who can reach the young crescent, it becomes a thread-ladder for the ready mind.
296.nuance: நூலேணி puns on rope ladder and ladder of texts. இளமதி may be the crescent on Siva's head or the moon centre of yogic practice; நெருப்பு and மணி may also be yogic. The plain sense is that study, rightly used, leads up to him.

297.reading: Before the Lord who was companion on the way and medicine, the mind of the unlearned is cast aside; he of great nature, the one above, is the companion on the way through all seven worlds.
297.nuance: வழித்துணை and மருந்து are epithets of Siva; Sengalvaraya notes Sundarar's 'வழித்துணை மருந்தே' (Tevaram 7.70.9). கழித்துணை and ஒழித்துணை are unclear.

298.reading: If you would cling, cling to the Supreme; with the First One's grace all is fulfilled, and the learned, by the skill they have, stand in great bliss like the shining gods.
298.nuance: பற்றது பற்றில் plays on பற்று as Kural 350 does: attachment redirected, not abolished. கிற்ற விரகு (the skill one has) is unclear, and so is whether the shining gods are a comparison or what the learned become.

299.reading: He who owns the sea and the mountain, whose body is the five elements, the lord of the immortals who rides the mighty bull through age after age, dwells in the hearts of those who have room for him.
299.nuance: இடமுடையார் is those with room in their hearts; it may also pun on those who own land. The Lord who owns the sea and mountains chooses the heart as his dwelling.

links.note: Both give the learned eyes. The Kural says the unlearned have two sores for eyes; Tirumular places an eye in the thought of the learned.
Both make learning something that goes with a person: the Kural through seven births, Tirumular as a companion, without saying how far.
Both turn attachment toward the Lord: the Kural says cling to the one free of clinging in order to let go, Tirumular says if you would cling, cling to the Supreme.
252 asks of everyone a leaf for God; 292 makes such worship of his feet the content of learning itself.

source_issues: 293: lines 1 and 2 (கல்வியுடையார் கழிந்தோடிப் போகின்றார் / பல்லியுடையார் பாம்பரிந்து உண்கின்றார்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
291: line 4 (கற்றறி காட்டக் கயல்உள வாக்குமே) is obscure.
